questions.q: What problem does MCP solve?
options: Every AI app needing its own integration for every tool
questions.why: One MCP server per tool, usable by any MCP host: N + M instead of N × M.

questions.q: Your Spring AI app connects to an MCP server. Which role does your app play?
questions.why: The host is the AI app; it contains one client per server connection.

questions.q: Who decides when a resource is read?
questions.why: Tools are model-controlled, resources app-controlled, prompts user-controlled.

questions.q: Which transport starts the server as a local process?
questions.why: stdio: the host launches the server and talks through its standard input and output.

questions.q: How do MCP tools reach your ChatClient in Spring AI?
options: They are added to the system prompt
questions.why: The MCP client starter exposes every server tool as a normal tool callback.

questions.q: Which annotation publishes a method as an MCP tool?
In the lab, /mcp returned 404 at first. Why?
options: The server used the older SSE transport by default; protocol=STREAMABLE fixed it
questions.why: spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol=STREAMABLE exposes the Streamable HTTP endpoint /mcp.

questions.q: find_order only reads data. What should you add?
questions.why: Without hints, the lab's tools were marked destructive by default.

questions.q: What does the server return first in a session, besides its capabilities?
questions.why: Every following request sends that session id.

questions.q: 'Only PROCESSING orders can be cancelled' belongs...
options: In Java code inside the tool
questions.why: Descriptions guide the model; Java enforces the rule for every client.

questions.q: In MCP's OAuth model, the MCP server is...
questions.why: It accepts requests only with a valid token from a trusted authorization server.

questions.q: A request without a token gets 401 and a WWW-Authenticate header. What does it point to?
options: The protected resource metadata, listing trusted authorization servers
questions.why: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource lets clients discover where to get tokens.

questions.q: A backend app calls the MCP server for itself, with no user. Which grant type?
questions.why: The lab used client_credentials with a client id and secret.

questions.q: What adds the token to every MCP request in the lab's client?
questions.why: It gets (and caches) a token and sets Authorization: Bearer.

questions.q: The client started with a wrong secret. What happened?
options: It failed to start: invalid_client from the token endpoint
questions.why: The MCP client connects at startup, so a bad credential stops the app.

challenge.title: An MCP server for a library catalogue
challenge.task: Build an MCP server over Streamable HTTP for a library: books, members and loans in memory. Connect a Spring AI client that answers questions like 'Is Dune available?' and 'Borrow Dune for member M-12'.
requirements: Tools: search_books (read-only hint), borrow_book and return_book; a member can't borrow more than 3 books, checked in Java
A resource library://rules with the loan rules, and a prompt 'overdue-reminder' with a memberId argument
Test every tool, the resource and the prompt with curl (or mcp.sh) before connecting a model
Secure the server with OAuth 2 client credentials; borrow and return require the scope library.write
A Spring AI client with a tool-capable model, getting its token automatically
selfCheck: A request without a token gets 401
A client with only library.read can search but not borrow
The 4th loan is refused by Java, whatever the model says
